title: Disjoint Sets
summary: A **disjoint set** groups items so code can ask whether two items are connected.
refresher: A **disjoint set** uses `find` to locate a group representative and `union` to merge groups. It is strong for connectivity, components, and cycle checks.

blocks.prompt: Which debugging habit fits disjoint sets best?
choices: Trace one small state change before trying a larger input
Start with the largest hidden case
Change the data structure after each failed test
Ignore the saved state and read only the final answer
blocks.why: The representative is the evidence. If you compare raw parents too early, a compressed path can make the trace look wrong.

sections.title: Common disjoint-set mistakes
sections.summary: Union code often reports a merge even when both values already share a representative. That inflates component changes.
